newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods ease as NYMEX scares buyers.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods ease as NYMEX scares buyers.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices were generally lower in spotty Tuesday activity, as wide swings in the NYMEX markets scared buyers out of the market, traders said.
"People aren't going to be doing much," a broker said.
After trading as high as 60.20 cents a gallon, heating oil for March delivery slid to 59.50 cents in late New York markets.
Meanwhile, crude saw volatility, with March contracts bouncing back from a morning low of $21.89 cents to trade $22.57 a barrel, up 16 cents from Friday's settle.
Bids for conventional unleaded gasoline were talked two cents lower in Los Angeles at 68 cents. Bids for CARB material rose one cent to 74 cents, but offers stayed flat at 75 cents.
L.A. distillates retreated Tuesday, with low sulphur diesel bids off one penny to 71 cents.
